releases.name: Anka 1.0.1
releases.body:
**Anka 1.0.1** opens games stored as **.nup** packages.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `2d17a71ff0f0cf0c27b3d7207818fade9199b77b`; both programs carry this commit.

## Updating from 1.0.0

Close Anka, unzip **`Anka-1.0.1-win64.zip`** into your Anka folder and replace the files. Your `user` folder (settings, keys, firmware and saves) stays as it is.

New to Anka: follow the quick start in the [1.0.0 notes](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/releases/tag/anka-v1.0.0). Unzip into a new, empty folder, start `anka.exe`, and install your own keys and firmware.

## What's in 1.0.1

### .nup packages
- `.nup` ("Unencrypted (Archival) Package") is a container format from upstream Eglantine. It holds one title's base game, update and add-on content in a single file.
- Anka now **reads** .nup files. You can open them with **File › Load File…**, and they appear in the game list with their icon, name and version. `anka-cli.exe` and its launchers open them too, including from the `Games` folder.
- Mods (LayeredFS) and Anka's game-specific settings apply to games opened from a .nup, the same as for other formats. Anka finds the title ID before the game starts.

releases.name: Anka 1.0.0
releases.body:
First release of **Anka**, a Nintendo Switch 2 emulator for Windows, focused on performance.

Built from [`anka`](https://github.com/EddizEge/Anka/tree/anka) at `b7542ece8b5c695e2f01d5e46b74c0806d48ae96`; both programs carry this commit.

## Quick start

1. Unzip **`Anka-1.0.0-win64.zip`** into a **new, empty folder**. Do not unzip it into another emulator's folder: its Qt DLLs would replace that program's.
2. Start **`anka.exe`**. Anka keeps its settings, keys, firmware and saves in the `user` folder next to it (portable mode) and does not touch `%APPDATA%\eden` or other installs.
3. Install your own keys and firmware as with other Eden-based emulators. Anka includes no games, keys or firmware; only use what you legally own.
4. Settings: **Emulation › Configure… › Anka**. The first start picks *Recommended*, the setup we measured (with GPU Mode *Fast*, the default; it also turns Reactive Flushing off).

Coming from PokeDinner-Eglantine 2.0.0: back up its `nand` folder (your saves), then copy its `user` folder next to `anka.exe`.

Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a current Vulkan driver. Qt and the Visual C++ runtime come with Anka.

## What's in 1.0.0

## XMB mode

**The PS3's own menu.** ARMSX3 can now look and work like the PS3's XMB: the wave and sparkles, the boot, every column with its rows and settings, music with the Waves, Valley and Gaia visualizers, a video player, a photo viewer with slideshows, the XMB keyboard, and the in-game XMB with save states, Change Disc and Turn Off System. releases.body:
Changes since 0.0.1. Thanks to everyone who sent problem reports, since most of these fixes came from them. This is a beta: the JIT changes ran on an iPhone, and everything else was tested on a Mac. Please send a report if something works worse than in 0.0.1.

## Requirements and install

ARMSX3 for iOS needs an iPhone or iPad with an A14 chip or newer, on iOS 17.4 or later. It isn't on the App Store, so install the IPA with SideStore, AltStore or LiveContainer. JIT needs a pairing file for your device (see Pairing files below).

## Update LiveContainer first

If you run ARMSX3 inside LiveContainer, update LiveContainer to 3.8.13 or later before you install this build. That is the nightly build at the moment: https://github.com/LiveContainer/LiveContainer/releases/tag/nightly Older versions can't load the JIT helper, and ARMSX3 will fall back to StikDebug.

In LiveContainer, turn on Helper Process Support for ARMSX3, and open ARMSX3 full screen, not in a window.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.6.7
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.6.7 Most of this release is @J1coding's work: fixes he found while bringing ARMSX3 to iOS, now on Android too. ## New - **Faster boots**: ARMSX3 now keeps a game's compiled SPU code between boots. The first boot after an update builds it once, and every boot after that loads it. On an Odin 3, Spider-Man: Web of Shadows' SPU step takes 2.5 s instead of 16 s. It lives in ARMSX3's own cache folder on the phone, which Android can clear like any app cache, and it switches itself off when the phone has less than 1 GB free. Done by @J1coding. ## Rare-case fixes - **Leaving a game no longer gets stuck** on memory the graphics side had locked. Done by @J1coding.

releases.body:
## Persona 5 Royal Android Recomp v0.5.13

### Español
- **Optimizaciones universales NVN/Android y FSR 1.0 (PR #263):** Reducción de permutaciones de pipeline con EDS1-3, precompilación de shaders en segundo plano, pooling de staging/spill buffers, aislamiento en núcleos grandes y caché de vistas `HandleSlot` entre shaders.
- **Nuevas opciones en el Launcher (PR #264):** Añadidos toggles para escalado **FSR 1.0 (`NX_FSR`)** y **sombras bajas para Mali (`NX_MALI_LOW_SHADOWS`)**.
- **Vibración en mando físico y dispositivo (PR #252):** Soporte de rumble/vibración en Android.
- **Fix Android 10 (API 29) (#258):** Guard para `InsetsController` en dispositivos por debajo de Android 11 con fallback seguro a modo inmersivo clásico.
- **Diagonales en mando físico (#255) y swapchain FSR:** Zona muerta radial 2D para alcanzar el 100% en diagonales y resolución nativa de swapchain preservada cuando `NX_FSR=1`.

---

### English
- **Universal NVN/Android optimizations & single-pass FSR 1.0 (PR #263):** EDS1-3 pipeline permutation reduction, background shader prewarm, staging spill buffer pooling, big-core thread isolation, and cross-shader `HandleSlot` view caching.

releases.name: v0.5.12: Hide controls option, Play crash hotfix & GPU hang fixes
releases.body:
## Persona 5 Royal Android Recomp v0.5.12

### Español
- **Ocultar controles en pantalla:** Se añadió la opción en el Launcher (`NX_TOUCH_HIDE`) para ocultar los controles visuales. Los controles siguen 100% activos y funcionales al tocar la pantalla, ideal para quienes prefieren la pantalla limpia o juegan con memoria muscular.
- **Corrección de cierre inmediato al iniciar (Play crash):** Se protegió el acceso a JNI y verificación de permisos de almacenamiento en `android_main` para dispositivos cargando directo por NSP/FD (POCO X7 Pro, POCO F6, etc.).
- **Solución al congelamiento en "Preparing game":** Se limitaron los hilos del compilador de shaders a un máximo de 4 durante la importación, solucionando bloqueos indefinidos en procesadores MediaTek Dimensity 8350.
- **Corrección de cuelgues de GPU (GPU Hangs):** Se deshabilitaron las divisiones de renderpass a mitad de pase (`NX_CHUNK_IN_PASS=0`) por defecto en GPUs TBDR (Adreno 830 / Mali).
- **Corrección de texto en mensajes (IM / SNS Chat):** Se corrigió el renderizado del texto en las opciones de respuesta del chat del teléfono móvil (PR #251).

releases.name: v0.5.11: Audio resume, UI pipeline state & Qualcomm movie alignment fixes
releases.body:
## Persona 5 Royal Android v0.5.11

### Fixes & Improvements / Correcciones y mejoras
- **Audio resume on sleep/lock screen (Fixes #238):**
  Automatically recreates the AAudio stream when disconnected, restoring game sound upon waking or unlocking the phone.
  *Se re-crea automáticamente el flujo de audio de AAudio al desconectarse, restaurando el sonido del juego al desbloquear o reanudar el teléfono.*
- **UI stripes and color banding on tile-based GPUs (Fixes #243):**
  Fixed bound pipeline and dynamic state cache invalidation on render pass end, preventing dull colors and white stripes in menus and dialogue on Adreno, Mali, and PowerVR.
  *Se corrigió la invalidación del estado dinámico y pipelines al finalizar un pase de renderizado, solucionando colores apagados y franjas blancas en la interfaz.*

releases.name: Def Jam v1.3 — Discord, Voice & Controls Update
releases.body:
Def Jam v1.3 brings Discord account integration, room discovery corrections, voice chat, refreshed menus and restored custom analog controls to the Android ARM64 port.

## Online and Discord
- Sign in through the official FFNY Online Discord account service. New connections use the verified account name; the manual player-name screen is removed.
- Saved sessions use encrypted app-private storage. Account sign-out, deletion and privacy controls remain accessible inside the game.
- Fixed the PC build fingerprint used for ordinary room and player discovery. The missing build-number bytes previously separated Android players from compatible PC lobbies.
- Choose Europe or North America from the launcher. Both players must use the same region.
- Added real account statistics and leaderboard access in the native online menu.
- Preserved room codes, native room creation, fighter selection and the existing online flow.

## Room voice chat
- Added PC-compatible room voice with push-to-talk: enable voice, allow microphone access and hold MIC to speak.
- Added a microphone permission prompt on first game entry, playback volume and a Mute/Unmute microphone button.

releases.name: Def Jam v1.2 — Controls & Compatibility Update
releases.body:
Update for the Android ARM64 port, focused on controls, frame pacing and online compatibility.

## Changes since v1.1
- Expanded Xbox/PlayStation-style and custom touch control layouts, including dual analog input and editable menu buttons.
- Improved the online player-name prompt and retained the original in-game online menu with room codes. Removed the extra floating ONLINE shortcut; Enter/Start is retained.
- Updated automatic 60 FPS menu / 30 FPS low-end combat pacing, frame-time statistics and CPU/network diagnostics. Actual performance depends on the device and scene.
- Reduced repeated missing-file lookups and refined online input waiting and delay handling.
- Updated the public relay connection handshake and corrected misleading password errors and repeated connection attempts after rejection.
- Included experimental, opt-in rollback support. It is not certified for stable cross-device play and respects the relay's rollback permission.

Existing saves, the built-in ISO/XISO extractor, gamepad support, English/Portuguese/Spanish interfaces and asynchronous Vulkan rendering are retained.

- Original (F1) and Remaster (F4) presentation modes.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.4
releases.body:
Fixes for the games reported on GitHub, PlayStation controllers, and the
Master System's Light Phaser and paddle.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.4-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### New

- **PlayStation controllers.** A DualShock 4 or DualSense is recognised and
  laid out like an Xbox pad, with its own button names in the Input tab. A
  DualShock 3 works through DsHidMini.
- **Automatic controller choice.** GenX uses whatever pad is plugged in, and
  the keyboard when there's none. New installs start on it; pick it in
  **Configure → Input** if you already have settings.
- **Master System Light Phaser and Paddle Control**, aimed with the mouse,
  plugged in by themselves for the games that need them.
- **Light gun games get their gun by themselves**, on the Mega Drive and the
  Sega CD.

### Fixed

- **Pier Solar** now plays and saves.
- **Back to the Future Part III (Europe)** starts on the Master System and
  the Mega Drive. Other European games that need a 50Hz console get one.
- **50Hz games no longer run 20% fast**, including Fantastic Dizzy.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.3
releases.body:
Play your real Sega CD discs. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.3-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### New

- **Sega CD discs straight from your PC's CD/DVD drive.** Put the disc in,
  choose **File → Open ROM → Sega CD from drive**, and pick the drive. GenX
  reads the game and its CD music from the disc, reading ahead while you play
  so the drive keeps up. A USB drive works too.
- **Changing discs:** use **Sega CD → Swap to disc in drive**, or just put the
  next disc in the drive. GenX swaps it in as a real Sega CD would.
- **Front ends:** `genx.exe E:\` starts the disc in drive E:.

You still need the Sega CD BIOS for the disc's region.

If your drive or a disc doesn't work, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/issues) with the drive's
make and model and the game.

See the [changelog](https://github.com/GamesExObscura/GenX/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
for every change.

Windows may show a SmartScreen warning because the exe isn't code-signed.
Choose **More info → Run anyway**.

releases.name: GenX v1.1.2
releases.body:
Sega CD fixes. Nothing else in the emulation changed.

**Download:** `GenX-v1.1.2-win64.zip`. Unzip it anywhere and run `genx.exe`.
To update, replace your old `genx.exe` with the new one. Your settings and
saves stay where they are.

### Fixed

- **Crash when opening a Sega CD disc.** GenX closed without a message when a
  disc sat near a file or folder whose name has certain characters, such as an
  accent stored as a separate mark (some "Pokémon" names) or Japanese text.
- **Japanese and Southeast Asian Sega CD BIOSes now start.** They used to stop
  on an error such as "This is a PAL-compatible Mega CD for exclusive use in
  Southeast Asia", because GenX always presented itself as a US or European
  console. GenX now becomes the console the BIOS belongs to.
- **Japanese discs get a Japanese BIOS** when your BIOS folder also holds the
  Southeast Asian one. Some BIOS packs name the Southeast Asian BIOS
  `jp_mcd1_9112.bin`, which GenX used to pick first.
- The **BIOS** tab in **Configure** shows the BIOS each region's discs will
  really use.

Thanks to the player who reported the Southeast Asia error.

releases.body:
## Added NetPlay Public Rooms

Until now, NetPlay worked over the internet with no account, no relay, and no service to trust. The one thing it could not do was find you an opponent: you still had to know someone already, and swap an IP address with them by hand.

**Public Rooms** is that missing half. It's an optional board where hosts advertise the game they are hosting, so anyone with the same ROM can tap it and connect.

What it is *not* is a relay. The board introduces two players and then steps out of the way — the match still runs directly between the two devices, exactly as it did before, and nothing about it passes through any server of mine. 

### On the board

* **Room codes.** Every room gets a short code you can pass to a friend. 
* **PIN rooms.** Tick *Require PIN* and the room still appears, marked as protected, but only the people you told can get in. The PIN itself never reaches the server — only a hash of it does.
* **A color-coded connection forecast.** Green, amber, or red per room, based on what STUN actually measured about both routers rather than a guess. Two symmetric NATs with no way through show red and refuse the join.

## 1.37 NetPlay

All of CPS-3 does: 3rd Strike and the earlier two, JoJo's Bizarre Adventure,
Red Earth. Until now these were stuck in Lockstep, which is the worst place for

**Console Five Pro v0.0.9proQ4** — an independent rebranded build of CapyPS5 v0.0.3, the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android (built on KytyPS5 and the FEX x86-64 JIT).

## v0.0.9proQ4 — the freeze fix, the after-freeze crash, frame flow in heavy 3D (same graphics)
- **Fixed: the multi-second freezes.** A draw whose pipeline was still compiling used to block the renderer with an *unbounded* wait on the compile queue. A storm of first-visit pipelines (a new area, material streaming, one-shot LUT passes) could then park the whole renderer behind the workers for tens of seconds - the field logs show 14-28 s of frozen video and starved audio right before the session died. No draw waits more than `debug.capy.pipeline_wait_ms` (default 4 ms, 0 = never wait) now: past the bound the draw is skipped, the compile lands in the background, and the next occurrence draws for real. Every pipeline miss is queued to the async workers - the renderer never compiles inline during play.

What's new in 0.78

For players
- **32-bit devices:** one APK now holds both ARMv8 (arm64-v8a) and ARMv7
  (armeabi-v7a). Android picks the right one on install, so 64-bit devices
  always run the 64-bit version. OpenGL ES 3.0 is still required.
- **Screen orientation:** the setting now applies to the launcher as well as
  the game and takes effect at once. Auto respects the system rotation lock.
- **Sound:** the audio buffer margin now adapts to the device.
- **Launcher:** new Advanced screen with a Debug mode switch. With it off,
  nothing is written to the log.
- **Logs:** new screen under Data to export, share or send logs to the
  developer, or clear them.

Under the hood
- **Most of the game is now ported C++:** - game code is moving from recompiled to ported native ARM code.
- **Old processor code removed:** x87 emulation is gone from the generated
  code, and the whole game runs in 24-bit floating point. MMX, CPU detection
  and the Pentium FDIV workarounds are removed too.

Known limits
- ARMv7 has only been tested in the 32-bit mode of a 64-bit phone, not on a
  real 32-bit device, so speed on older hardware is unknown.

### Added
- The installer shows its version (the game's tag, or the short commit for a
  build off a branch) in the window's corner and title, and on start asks
  GitHub for the game's newest release: a newer one gets a download button.
  Offline it says nothing.

  game, for a title whose setup takes an image rather than an install.

  the game's folder or a folder holding a zip of it.

  has `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so antivirus heuristics and players can check it.
- A log of why the installer stopped (`%APPDATA%\recomp-launcher\launcher.log`
  on Windows), and an error box instead of the window vanishing.

### Fixed
- On Windows a step line after a blank line was glued to the line before it
  (ConPTY skips the blank line with a cursor move), so the bar missed that step.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc8
releases.body:
This release candidate completes support for the cheat instructions implemented by Eden's DMNT engine and improves cheat-file parsing and process targeting.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc7.

### What's new since rc7

- **Extended cheat instructions:** implemented register comparisons, register save/restore operations and masks, persistent static registers, process pause/resume, and debug logging, with all operand and addressing forms supported by Eden.
- **Cheat execution:** corrected nested if/else handling, loop decoding, arithmetic behavior, and handling of truncated or unknown instructions. Controller input is sampled once per execution so multiple button conditions see the same input state.
- **Cheat files and process targeting:** fixed parsing of names containing Unicode symbols or accents. Memory operations and pause/resume now target the process identified by the cheat metadata, with a cached non-owning process reference.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc7
releases.body:
This release candidate fixes several cheat-engine decoding errors, adds missing process-memory service calls, and addresses an applet command that caused some game to abort.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc6.

### What's new since rc6

- **Cheat execution:** corrected data widths, register selection, immediate values, and pointer-chain offsets. These errors could prevent loaded cheats from taking effect.
- **Process-memory services:** wired `SetProcessMemoryPermission`, `MapProcessMemory`, and `UnmapProcessMemory` into both ARM64 and ARM32 system-call dispatch. Aligned permission handling and validation order with Eden, with tests for writable aliases, unmapping, and error handling. This addresses missing calls needed by injected cheat modules; end-to-end compatibility with third-party CheatVM modules is not yet verified.
- **Applet compatibility:** added Eden's success response for `ILibraryAppletAccessor` command 90. Also implemented `GetLibraryAppletInfo` to return the child applet's identity and mode.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc6
releases.body:
This release candidate fixes an audio-update parsing error that could cause invalid mixer data and audio glitches.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes all improvements from rc1 through rc5.

### What’s new since rc5

- **Audio update parsing:** the audio renderer now respects the splitter block size declared in the update header. Previously, it could read the following mixer block at the wrong offset, resulting in invalid mix counts or rejected audio updates.
- **Input validation:** added bounds checks for declared splitter blocks.
- **Regression coverage:** added synthetic tests covering splitter block boundaries, subsequent mixer updates, and header layout.

This correction addresses a likely cause of the audio errors reported in [issue #21](https://github.com/vricosti/ruzu-emu/issues/21). Confirmation through extended gameplay is still needed.

### Known limitations

Unsupported shader instructions may still cause missing graphics or prevent a scene from rendering. This release does not resolve every freeze, black-screen issue, or audio glitch.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc5
releases.body:
**This release candidate improves shader error handling, Windows build support, and diagnostics for freezes and black screens.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes the improvements from rc1 through rc4.

### What’s new since rc4

- **Shader stability:** unsupported shader instructions now produce an error that the Vulkan pipeline compiler can handle, rather than terminating the GPU worker. This improves error recovery but does not add support for those instructions.
- **Graphics compatibility:** aligned constant-buffer and texture validation with Eden and corrected how constant-buffer values are recorded for shader caching.
- **Windows memory handling:** aligned unsupported memory-protection handling with Eden, avoiding an unconditional panic.
- **Windows builds:** improved detection of existing Visual Studio installations and installation of missing C++ tools. Runtime DLLs are now copied alongside the build binaries, and a vcpkg compatibility fix was added.

releases.name: Ruzu v0.1.1-rc4
releases.body:
This release candidate adds support for multi-program titles such as game collections and fixes an ordering problem in kernel thread termination.

**This is a pre-release for testing before v0.1.1.** Feedback and reproducible bug reports are welcome. It includes the improvements from rc1, rc2 and rc3.

### What’s new since rc3

- **Game collections:** titles that chain into a sub-program (`ExecuteProgram`) now work. Previously, picking a game from a collection’s menu left the screen frozen at 0 FPS. Ruzu now shuts the running program down and boots the requested program of the same file. 
- **Kernel:** thread termination now signals completion and notifies waiting threads under the scheduler lock, after the terminating thread has left its core. This closes an ordering window between the two notifications.

### Known limitations

Only the collection listed above was tested with the new sub-program launch path. Other multi-program titles may still expose missing behavior, and reports are welcome.

releases.body:
# Bloodborne PC 1.9.8.6

What's new since 1.9.8.4.

## Picture fixes
- **Smeared picture fixed (two causes):**
  - After a load, the game sometimes rewrote a command buffer it had already handed to the GPU. The picture then stayed broken or smeared until the game was restarted. Every submitted command buffer is now copied first (`BB_COPY_GPU_BUFFERS=0` turns this off). The same cause was behind "Unimplemented PM4 type 0" and "PM4 header ... rest of the buffer dropped" in logs.
  - After a start with an empty shader cache, one saved pipeline could be lost for the whole next session. The game's motion blur then kept blurring the last frame, so the picture looked smeared and frozen from the first camera turn on.
- Rainbow tiles on hit enemies and a light line along the top in cutscenes are fixed.

# 🛡️ [MOD] Exiled Kingdoms LAN Multiplayer — 2.0!

Hey everyone! Another update to the **LAN Multiplayer** mod for Exiled Kingdoms.

Here's the full summary:

---

## ⚔️ NEW — LAN Multiplayer Bug Fixes

### 🐛 Bug: Crash when entering Cities
- **Problem:** When entering some cities, the game would crash and close.
- **Fix:** Problem fixed, and you can now teleport and enter cities perfectly.

### 🐛 Bug: Monsters ignored the CLIENT when the HOST was far away
- **Problem:** Monsters only attacked when the HOST was nearby. If only the CLIENT approached, the monster would remain still.
- **Fix:** Detection now compares the HOST and all CLIENTs present on the same map and returns the **closest** to the monster as the target.

### 🐛 Bug: Incorrect monster level scaling in co-op
- **Problem:** Monsters scaled based on 0+ (extra players). × 2), resulting in level 2 Goblins in a session with 2
- **Correction:** Now uses the Bestiary's `minlevel` as a base before applying the LAN difficulty multiplier. Example: Goblin (base level 4) + 2 players = level 6. Yeti (base level 18) + 2 players = level 22.

### 🐛 Bug: CLIENT couldn't reduce HOST's HP in the PVP Arena

releases.name: v0.10.65 — Rocky Ridge minecart above 60 Hz: the lever and the jump into the cart

releases.name: v0.10.64 — Expert courses above 60 Hz: the Final Factory skydive and the Metropolis Speedway launch
releases.body:

- **Expert courses above 60 Hz (#410).** With **Test options › Gameplay › Race step rate** above 60 (for example 120 or 144):

  - **Metropolis Speedway Expert:** the launch up the building no longer hangs at the top. At 144 Hz the racer stayed up there about 5.5 seconds instead of 3; it is now about 3.7 seconds.
  - Both were parts of the course that moved the racer by a fixed amount each step, written for steps of one frame; they now move by the right amount for shorter steps. At the default 60 Hz nothing changes.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.63](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.63).

releases.name: v0.10.63 — Older Mali phones no longer stop with a graphics error
releases.body:
## Changes

- **Older Mali phones (#406).** On phones with an older ARM Mali graphics chip, such as the Galaxy A05 and A06 (Mali-G52), the game no longer stops at start with "native graphics pipeline creation failed".
  - Their graphics driver refused every way of drawing a textured surface the game prepares, because of one feature the game asked for. The game now draws textures in a way that does not need it, and costs nothing extra.
  - Other phones, tablets and computers draw exactly as before.

Everything else is the same as [v0.10.62](https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled/releases/tag/v0.10.62).

## Validation

- **Galaxy A06 (Mali-G52, the same chip as the A05), the fix's own build:** the graphics self test prepared all 455 ways of drawing (0.10.62: 71), drew with every one of them and read the picture back. This release's APK itself was not run on a Mali device.
- **AYN Thor (Adreno), this release's APK:** the same graphics self test prepared all 455 with none skipped and drew with all of them, so nothing changed on Adreno.

**Nixport v1.2.304-alpha** — a test build for people who want to try it early.

> Published by hand: built and signed with the same key as v1.1.299-alpha and

## Changelog (since v1.1.299-alpha)

### Gamepads

- **Single-player pad model** (replaces v1.1's player slots): exactly one physical
  pad feeds the game at a time. The pad you touch takes over automatically
  (last-active wins); the session drawer offers "use this pad" to pin a choice for
  the session. The effective pad and the on-screen controls merge into one player.
- **Fix: intermittent directional input**. After opening a menu or losing focus,
  sticks / D-pad / triggers now reach the game immediately at their current position —
  no more "only X works in the load screen" or "the first press does nothing".
  The old "stay blocked until centered" gate is gone (keys only).
- Rumble now always lands on the effective pad (Xbox-protocol pads don't expose
  motors to Android — enable "phone vibration" as the fallback).
- On-screen stale-state fix: a closed overlay can no longer pin the virtual stick
  over the physical one.

releases.name: MarathonRecomp-Android v0.2.4
releases.body:
**A test release: one rendering change for tile-based GPUs and two new log lines.** ARM64, Android 10 (API 29) or newer, Vulkan. Installs over v0.2.3 and keeps your saves.

## Changes

- **The final pass no longer loads the screen image first.** The last pass of every frame (gamma and rotation) draws every pixel of the screen image, so its old contents are not read back any more. This matters on tile-based GPUs: Mali, and Adreno with the stock driver or Turnip in GMEM mode. How much time it saves is **not measured yet** — that is what this release is for. It follows the launcher switch *Optimized render passes (Vulkan)*: with the switch off the image is loaded as before.
- **`[fps]` line in every log.** Once a minute `log.txt` gets a line with the frame rate, the average and the worst frame time, the number of frames longer than 100 ms and 1 s, GPU time, render scale and the FPS cap. *Performance log* does not have to be on for it.

releases.name: Pocket Foundry 0.9.2
releases.body:
Play your own copy of Factorio on Android: the official Linux ARM64 build, run without emulation on the phone's GPU.

**Install:** open `pocket-foundry-0.9.2.apk` on the phone (Android 10 or later) and import the Linux (arm64) .tar.xz from [factorio.com/download](https://factorio.com/download). Pocket Foundry then asks before downloading a driver for your GPU from pocket-foundry-drivers: Turnip on Adreno 6xx or newer, experimental builds on some Mali and Xclipse GPUs, Phone's OpenGL ES (MobileGlues) or the CPU elsewhere. Without downloads it plays through Phone's Vulkan (experimental) or an imported one. The app holds no part of Factorio: you bring your own copy. A new version installs over the last and keeps the game and saves; from 0.8, 0.9 installs as a new app next to the old one and brings its saves, mods and config over.

**Updates:** Pocket Foundry doesn't check for them itself. Add it to [Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) with this repository's link, and Obtainium installs each new version. Coming from 0.8, remove the old Pocket Foundry in Obtainium and add it again: 0.9 is a new app.

✅ **The phone builds its shaders too**: when you add the game and on every **Update game**, from the game's own files. Nothing from the game is downloaded or shipped with the app.
✅ **You can switch back**: the game's **Settings → Renderer → Xenia** brings back the emulation.

## Updating a game

✅ **Coming from 0.1.1:** Use **Update game** (⋮ on the game's card) on each game once. State of Decay gets its new profile and builds its shader library for the native renderer; the game files, saves and settings stay.
